title: component_of over many paths walks component_dirs once
intention: address gains components_of(paths), which answers component_of for every path with one walk of component_dirs, so a caller over a closure pays one walk instead of one per file.
why: Measured 2026-11-12: the home bus wedged at 100% of one core with codemother's traffic starving. py-spy put the CPU in validation_store calling address.component_of once per closure file; each call re-walks 77 components (~8.5 ms), 2.66 s over 300 files.
traces_to: Law 1 (the settled component set is re-derived per path, a defect) and the bus intention (a wake never takes more than 60 s).
how: Factor component_of's owner loop into _deepest_owner over pre-resolved component dirs; component_of uses it with one walk, components_of walks once and maps every path through it. Red-first proof: agreement with component_of, and one component_dirs call for 40 paths.

clauses.claim: components_of(paths) answers, for every path, exactly what component_of answers for it, including None for a path under no component
components_of over 40 paths calls component_dirs exactly once

decisions.text: D1: _deepest_owner(target, resolved) holds the deepest-ancestor rule; component_of and the new components_of(paths, pkg_root=None) -> dict both call it; the dict is keyed by each path as given.
D2: the red-first proof samples git ls-files paths plus one outside path for agreement, and counts component_dirs calls through a wrapper set for the call and restored after.

measured.saw: component_of ~8.5 ms a call, 20 calls 171.4 ms; component_dirs 77 components in 6.5 ms

measured.how: python3 timing over cairn.tools.base.address on akienasus
